title: Second look at N-006: DISSENT for now (scan confirmed; the published pairing could not be read, only seen in search summaries)
statement: Scan (canvas 1006196, crop 4850,1100,1300,700 and a close crop of the label at 5350,1350,200,100): every visual claim in N-006 holds. In the upper-left segment of the f68r3 wheel there is one tight cluster of exactly seven small stars, much smaller and closer together than any other star in the segment. A curved line runs from the cluster down and right to the ring around the central moon face. The word at f68r3.11 sits immediately right of the cluster on its baseline, oalcheol (f68r3.12) is written along the tail line, and dchol,day (f68r3.10) sits under the single large star to the left. At high zoom the label's last glyph is a closed loop with no descending stroke, which supports doaro (ZL3b, IT2a, LSI H and U) over doary (RF1b, LSI V); GC2a gives 8oay9. Relevant to N-006's open question: these are one locus, so a source that names 'doary' at the seven stars of f68r3 means this same word. Why I still dissent: N-006 asks second-lookers to agree only if Bax's paper confirms the word, or if a second independent published source pairs this label with the Pleiades or Taurus. I could not open any such source. stephenbax.net, voynichportal.com (the DoarusComment image), ic.unicamp.br (Stolfi's f68r3 notes) and voynich.ninja's other threads were refused by my network sandbox; only voynich.ninja thread 2102 opened, and its text quotes Bax on 'Taurus' and the seven stars without naming the word. A web search returned summaries saying that a post on Bax's site (https://stephenbax.net/?p=803, citing Marco Ponzi) calls EVA doary 'the label of the Pleiades in f68r3' and proposes it reads like Taurus, and that Stolfi's f68r3 notes (https://ic.unicamp.br/~stolfi/voynich/Notes/040/html/f68r3.htm) tentatively suggest doaro may mean the Pleiades. If those pages say this, the proposer's condition is met (two published sources, Bax/Ponzi and Stolfi, tie this label to the cluster). But I have only a search engine's paraphrase, not the pages, and a confirmed anchor feeds the test's criterion (c), so I do not agree on that basis. Recommendation: a second look that can open those two pages should check the quoted wording and, if it matches, agree; the identification of the cluster as the Pleiades remains an inference from the drawing, and Taurus as a name for the label is weaker than Pleiades.
